translations.answer: The original thread cannot support a general answer. Maintainers reproduced the issue on ANYmal, Spot, and Unitree, noting that the ImplicitActuatorCfg configuration is no longer present. However, the original questioner continued to encounter errors; the IMU linear acceleration from finite difference was bypassed, but the maintainers explicitly warned of noise. The team could not reproduce the issue in Isaac Sim 5.0. A comparison of actuator configuration, version, and independent acceleration reference should be conducted before selecting data sources.
translations.applicability: Applies to scenarios using explicit IdealPD classes for actuators and reading rigid-body acceleration in IsaacLab/Isaac Sim environments; version boundaries are not closed.
translations.credibility.rationale: The solution has not been closed or there are unresolved conflicts in the sources.
translations.details.attempts.0: Switch to ImplicitActuatorCfg; use IMU finite difference linear acceleration instead; upgrade/re-test Isaac Sim 5.0.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Compare actuator configuration and model; compare IdealPDActuator-derived models with ImplicitActuatorCfg; record body_acc_w and IMU finite difference linear acceleration; re-test in Isaac Sim 5.0.
translations.details.environments.0: Original post: ANYmal-C, dt=0.005, 2 environments, old omni.isaac.lab API; comments indicate reproduction covers Spot/Unitree; subsequent verification of Isaac Sim 5.0. Specific original submission not stated.
translations.details.limits.0: No thread provided final re-test by the original author for exact ImplicitActuatorCfg or Isaac Sim 5.0; cannot write any alternative as a universal fix.
translations.details.outcomes.0: Maintainers reproduced the original environment issue on multiple robots; ImplicitActuatorCfg is effective for the maintainers but not for the original questioner; team could not reproduce in Isaac Sim 5.0.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Robot is stationary but body_acc_w is significantly non-zero; does switching to another actuator model or Isaac Sim version resolve the issue?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Do not use body_acc to estimate external forces or trigger real-machine safety actions until the kinematic/finite difference kernels have been independently verified.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Collaborator observes the issue related to IdealPDActuator-derived actuators, but the original questioner's counterexample shows this explanation is not closed.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Base Z acceleration exceeds 5 when robot is stationary; removing joint position targets and writing causes robot to fall, with acceleration curve matching expectations.
translations.media_summaries.0: Original post contains abnormal and normal acceleration curves, but the maintainers have confirmed reproduction and conflict via text; this card does not extract additional numerical values from the curves.
translations.source.title: Abnormal body_acc_w in controlled stationary robots is conflicting between actuator model and version
translations.title: Can we directly switch to ImplicitActuatorCfg or use IMU readings in IsaacLab when body_acc_w is clearly wrong?
